at eksplodere.explanation: "At eksplodere" means "to explode". To say someone loses control of their feelings, use it for anger: "Han eksploderede af vrede" (He exploded with anger).

at eksportere.explanation: "At eksportere" means "to export". To say you send a file out of a program, use it with the file: "at eksportere en fil" (to export a file).

at elske.explanation: "At elske" means "to love". To tell a person you love them, say: "Jeg elsker dig" (I love you). To say you love a food, use the same verb: "Jeg elsker pizza" (I love pizza).

at ende.explanation: "At ende" means "to end". To say a story or event finishes a certain way, say: "Historien endte godt" (The story ended well). To say where you finally arrive, it also means "to end up": "Vi endte i Aarhus" (We ended up in Aarhus).

at ende med.explanation: "At ende med" means "to end up with". To name what you are left with, put a noun after it: "Jeg endte med en forkølelse" (I ended up with a cold). To say what you finally did, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Han endte med at købe en cykel" (He ended up buying a bike).

at enes.explanation: "At enes" means "to agree / get along". To say what people agree on, use "om" (about) after it: "Vi enedes om prisen" (We agreed on the price). To say people do not get along, add "ikke" (not): "De kan ikke enes" (They cannot get along).

at engagere sig.explanation: "At engagere sig" means "to get involved". To name what you get involved in, put "i" (in) before it: "Hun engagerer sig i den lokale idrætsklub" (She gets involved in the local sports club).

at erfare.explanation: "At erfare" means "to find out / experience". To name the fact you learned, add "at" (that) and a full sentence: "Jeg har erfaret, at toget er forsinket" (I have found out that the train is late).

at erklære.explanation: "At erklære" means "to declare". To say a country starts a war, say: "Landet erklærer krig" (The country declares war). To say you tell someone how you feel, use it with the feeling: "at erklære sin kærlighed" (to declare your love).

at erobre.explanation: "At erobre" means "to conquer". To say a company wins over customers, use it with the market: "at erobre markedet" (to conquer the market).

at erstatte.explanation: "At erstatte" means "to replace". To say you pay someone back for a loss, use it with the damage: "at erstatte en skade" (to compensate for damage).

at etablere.explanation: "At etablere" means "to establish". To say you set up your own place in a job or town, add "sig" (oneself): "Hun har etableret sig som tandlæge" (She has set herself up as a dentist).

at evakuere.explanation: "At evakuere" means "to evacuate". To name the place that is emptied, put it right after the verb: "at evakuere skolen" (to evacuate the school).

at evaluere.explanation: "At evaluere" means "to evaluate". To name what you judge, put it right after the verb: "Vi skal evaluere kurset" (We must evaluate the course).

e-boks.explanation: "En e-Boks" means "an e-Boks". It is the digital mailbox in Denmark where public offices, banks and companies send you letters. To tell someone to look for a letter, say: "Tjek din e-Boks" (Check your e-Boks).

eddike.explanation: "Eddike" means "vinegar". To say how much you add to a dish, use it with an amount: "en teskefuld eddike" (a teaspoon of vinegar).

effektiv.explanation: "Effektiv" means "efficient". When a remedy or tool works well, it also means "effective": "et effektivt middel" (an effective remedy).

efter.explanation: "Efter" means "after". When you search for something, it means "for": "at lede efter nøglerne" (to look for the keys). To put a whole sentence after "after", add "at" (that): "efter at jeg kom hjem" (after I came home).

efter min mening.explanation: "Efter min mening" means "in my opinion". It is built from "efter" (according to), "min" (my) and "en mening" (an opinion).

efterfølgende.explanation: "Efterfølgende" means "afterwards". It is built from "efter" (after) and "at følge" (to follow). When you name a day that comes next, put it before the noun, where it means "following": "den efterfølgende dag" (the following day).

efterhånden.explanation: "Efterhånden" means "gradually". When you say a feeling has built up over time, it means "by now": "Jeg er efterhånden træt af det" (I am getting tired of it by now).

efterhånden som.explanation: "Efterhånden som" means "as". To say one thing changes step by step while another goes on, use it before the clause: "Jeg bliver bedre, efterhånden som jeg øver" (I get better as I practice). To say two things only happen at the same time, use "mens" (while) instead: "Mens jeg øver, drikker jeg te" (While I practice, I drink tea).

efterlyst.explanation: "Efterlyst" means "wanted", as in a person the police are searching for. It comes from the verb "at efterlyse" (to put out a call for): "Politiet efterlyser vidner" (The police are asking for witnesses).

eftersom.explanation: "Eftersom" means "since", as in giving a reason. It is built from "efter" (after) and "som" (as).

efterspørgsel.explanation: "En efterspørgsel" means "a demand". To name what people want, add "på" after it: "efterspørgsel på billige boliger" (demand for cheap homes).
